description.narrative: Media development in the Eastern Partnership Region in order to increase the sustainability of independent MSMEs so they can offer access to information and employment. The fund offers grants based on a call off process that independent media organizations can be eligible.

Medieutveckling i den Östliga Partnerskapsregionen med syfte att öka hållbarheten för oberoende micro/små/medelstora medieorganisationer så att de kan bidra med information samt erbjuda arbetstillfällen. Fonden utlyser kravställda gåvostöd regelbundet som oberoende medieorganisationer kan söka.

sector.narrative: Media and free flow of information

description.narrative:
During the first year of cooperation, IFPIM has developed more transparent and efficient procedures, which has already resulted in them being able to ward off expected criticism in a convincing way and scale up the work.
Detailed and thorough monitoring instruments of grantees (enabling selection thereof and monitoring during the grantee periods) have been developed during the period. These are expected to have standards setting normative effect for the sector and also contribute to verifiable evidence on the media as such is not systematically performed by other actors in the region. This means that future polices can be better informed and reputation attacks mitigated based on facts. The findings can also inform the grantees self-promotion to audience and investors.
During the inception period, IFPIM has as an effect of the above been able to launch three calls for media support in the Estern Partnership region. This is already two more calls addressing the region than the year before the partnership with Sida. IFPIM already provide support to more than twice as many media outlets in the region compared to before this agreement, and in time for the upcoming parliamentary elections in Moldova late September, IFPIM had more than ten media partners in the country.
The total number of grantees in the recent reporting period was 39 (28 funded under Sida conditions. Outcome 1). Grantee economic resilience improved measurably across the portfolio, with 80% of outlets increasing both total and non-grant revenue, 80% retaining or growing staff, and 85% covering core costs despite the contextual funding decline 2025. (Outcomes 6 and 7). Content monitoring launched mid-year, established a baseline across five public interest dimensions; most sampled content met core professional standards (Outcome 5). Audience reach and engagement were maintained or increased by the majority/85% of grantees (Outcome 8). Content analysis identified a gender-sensitive framing gap (66%; Outcome 5), deeper insight into gaps of newsroom gender-inclusive policies and practices planned Y2
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
